turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung reassured O-lan that everything would be as she wished and that their eldest son would find a wife who would care for him well, though no one could match her own devotion.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan nodded, her eyes welling with tears, and told Wang Lung that she trusted him to guide their son and to take care of himself, for she would be watching over them from the other side.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son nodded, his eyes following the tears in his mother’s eyes, and he promised that he would always listen to his father’s guidance.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung nodded solemnly, his heart heavy with the weight of his wife’s words, and he promised her that he would guide their son as best he could, though he feared he might not have her strength.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan wiped her tears, her gaze shifting to her eldest son and the maid, and she urged them to make their marriage work, for their happiness was her greatest wish.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid bowed her head, her eyes downcast, and whispered softly to O-lan and the eldest son, assuring them that she would do her best to keep the family happy and fulfilled, for their peace was her highest concern.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son nodded, his eyes fixed on the maid, and he promised her that he would do his best to make her happy, though he felt a heavy burden weighing on his heart.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung looked at O-lan with a reassuring gaze, his heart heavy but his eyes full of hope, and he told her that he would see to it that their son and the maid would build a happy home, for their joy was her greatest wish.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan wiped her eyes again, her voice firm yet tinged with sorrow as she spoke, urging Wang Lung to take care of their son as she had taken care of them all, her wish clear and urgent.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung nodded, his eyes brimming with a mix of sadness and determination as he promised O-lan that he would care for their son as if he were his own flesh and blood, ensuring that the family would remain united and strong.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: She wiped her eyes again, her voice steady but sorrowful as she urged Wang Lung to ensure their son’s happiness, knowing her time was short.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung nodded, his voice steady but full of reassurance, telling O-lan that he would make sure their son found true happiness, for it was the least he could do to ease her worries.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: She urged Wang Lung to arrange the marriage of their son without delay, her eyes reflecting the urgency of her wish to see her son settled before she passed.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung nodded solemnly, his heart heavy with the responsibility she placed on him, assuring O-lan that he would arrange the marriage swiftly, for it was her last wish and he would not let her down.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: She urged Wang Lung to ensure the marriage was one that would bring happiness and stability to their son, her voice steady yet tinged with the weight of her impending departure.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: She moved quietly to offer a cup of water to O-lan, her eyes showing her concern and respect for the woman's wishes.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan nodded, her eyes never leaving Wang Lung, urging him to ensure the marriage would bring happiness and security to their son, for it was all she wished for before she left this world.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: He reassured O-lan, nodding solemnly, promising to find a suitable match for their son, one that would bring joy and stability to their family.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan watched Wang Lung closely, her expression softening as she pressed him to ensure their son was well cared for, knowing her time was short.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung nodded again, his voice low and reassuring, promising O-lan that he would take care of everything, and their son would be provided for and loved.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that there was another thing before she could die.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that she could not speak of dying and please him.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she must die, for she felt it in her vitals waiting, but she would not die before her eldest son came home and before he wed the good maid who was her daughter-in-law, and well she served her, holding the hot water basin steadily and knowing when to bathe her face when she sweated in pain. Now she wanted her son to come home, because she must die, and she wanted him to wed this maid first, so that she could die easily, knowing her grandson was stirred into life and a great grandson for the old one.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that she looked twice as well as they said and years away from death.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she would see him wed and then she must die.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung to sit here and drink the wine and eat the rice of his marriage, for she would see it all and this would be his bed of marriage since she was soon to be finished with it and carried away.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan asked Wang Lung if everyone had wine and if the sweet rice dish in the middle of the feast was very hot and if they had put full measure of lard and sugar into it and the eight fruits.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told her eldest son that she was now content and that he should look to his father and grandfather for guidance. She also instructed her daughter to observe her husband and his ancestors, pointing out the foolish woman in the court as an example of what not to do. O-lan insisted that her children had no duty to anyone else beyond these teachings.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan asked Wang Lung how that one could feed him and care for him as she did. Beauty would not bear a man sons!
